title: Trapped in Your Story: Evaluating Narrative-Induced Sycophancy in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.23525v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are known to exhibit sycophancy by adjusting their responses toward users' expressed views. However, real users often justify their opinions through reasons, personal experiences, causal explanations, and broader narratives, raising the question of whether such narratives can further steer model judgments. We construct a controlled benchmark of 500 debatable questions across ten domains, where the user stance is held fixed while its justification is systematically varied without introducing new task-relevant evidence. Each question is instantiated under 11 matched conditions: one neutral baseline and five mirrored narrative levels for each of two opposing positions, yielding 5,500 evaluation instances. We evaluate seven LLMs and observe substantial differences in narrative-induced agreement. translated_title: 困于你的故事：评估大语言模型中的叙事诱发谄媚行为
translated_abstract: 众所周知，大语言模型（LLM）会表现出谄媚（sycophancy）行为，即根据用户表达的观点来调整自己的回答。然而，现实中的用户往往会通过理由、个人经历、因果解释以及更广泛的叙事来为自己的观点辩护，这就引出了一个问题：此类叙事能否进一步引导模型的判断。我们构建了一个涵盖十个领域、包含500个可争论问题的受控基准，其中用户立场保持固定，而其论证方式被系统性地变化，且不引入任何新的与任务相关的证据。每个问题在11种匹配条件下进行实例化：一个中性基线条件，以及针对两种对立立场的各五个镜像叙事层级，共产生5,500个评估实例。我们评估了七个大语言模型，观察到叙事诱发的一致性存在显著差异。该效应并不随叙事的精细程度单调变化：个人经历可能降低一致性，而因果框架……（摘要在此处截断，原文不完整）
tldr: 该论文构建了一个包含500个问题、5,500个评估实例的受控基准，首次系统揭示大语言模型的判断会被用户的叙事性论证（如个人经历、因果解释）所左右，且这种“叙事诱发谄媚”效应并非随叙事精细程度单调增强。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a controlled benchmark of 500 debatable questions (5,500 evaluation instances) showing that LLM judgments can be steered by users' narrative justifications—such as personal experiences and causal explanations—even when stance and evidence are held fixed, and that this narrative-induced sycophancy effect is non-monotonic with narrative elaboration.
